\section[āmram]{\sk{आम्रम्} (āmram) — a mango}

\label{lesson:SA-C78-mango}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the roof, then the Sanskrit for a key.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आम्रम्}}
\textbf{\sk{आम्रम्}} (\emph{āmram}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mango\textquotedblright{}, the \textbf{\sk{फलम्}} of summer.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The summer fruit.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmram}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āmram}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for the roof, then the Sanskrit for a key, then say \emph{āmram} again
\end{itemize}

What does \sk{आम्रम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mango\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
